strings.name: Alfred Aho
strings.role: Computer scientist · Compiler and algorithm researcher
strings.summary: Trained at Toronto and Princeton, Aho researched languages, pattern matching and compilation at Bell Labs before teaching at Columbia. With collaborators he connected theory, UNIX tools and textbooks, helping create AWK and shaping computing education through algorithm and compiler books. In 2021 he and Jeffrey Ullman were named recipients of the 2020 Turing Award.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through 16 November 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: His work advanced algorithms, compilers and programming-language theory, influencing computing education and software engineering through books and tools.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: Engineering physics degree, University of Toronto; electrical engineering/computer science doctorate, Princeton.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Teaching compiler theory
strings.highlights.h1.text: Books with Ullman and other collaborators systematically linked programming languages to implementation and algorithms.
strings.highlights.h2.title: AWK and text-processing tools
strings.highlights.h2.text: He developed AWK with Brian Kernighan and Peter Weinberger and wrote early egrep and fgrep implementations.
strings.timeline.t1.title: New AWK book published
strings.timeline.t1.text: The second edition of The AWK Programming Language appeared under Aho, Kernighan and Weinberger's names.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Elected to the NAS
strings.timeline.t2.text: Elected for research in algorithms, programming languages and compilers.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Turing Award announced
strings.timeline.t3.text: ACM named him and Ullman joint recipients of the 2020 award for algorithms and theory underlying language implementation.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Joining Columbia
strings.timeline.t4.text: He moved into university research and teaching and also served as computer science department chair.
strings.timeline.t5.title: The compiler Dragon Book
strings.timeline.t5.text: He co-authored Compilers: Principles, Techniques, and Tools with Ravi Sethi and Ullman.
strings.timeline.t6.title: AWK and a compiler textbook
strings.timeline.t6.text: He helped develop AWK; Principles of Compiler Design, with Ullman, appeared the same year.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Collaboration at Bell Labs
strings.timeline.t7.text: He began a long collaboration with Ullman on language theory, implementation and algorithms.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Toronto degree
strings.timeline.t8.text: He completed engineering physics studies before pursuing graduate work at Princeton.
